headline: Nvidia takes $3 billion of Meta's share sale as Meta prices its stock at $625, HSBC drags the FTSE 100 down 0.9%, and SA's leading indicator turns up
summary: The rand was steady at R16.65/$ early on Tuesday with the 2035 bond yield at 8.62% (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 27 Oct), and the SARB's leading business cycle indicator rose 1.1% in August after falling 0.8% in July (Newsquawk, 27 Oct). Nvidia will buy $3 billion of Meta's equity offering, which Meta priced at $625 a share, below Monday's $642.70 close (TokenPost; Axios, 27 Oct), while the FTSE 100 fell 0.9% to 10,673 in early trade as HSBC slid after results (Share Talk, 27 Oct); the Fed decides on Wednesday. Brent eased 0.87% to $114.80 a barrel as diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war continue (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 27 Oct), and spot gold briefly slipped below $4,000 an ounce (TokenPost, 27 Oct).

items.title: Israel votes today in an election that decides Netanyahu's future
items.summary: Israelis elect the 26th Knesset on Tuesday 27 October; most polling stations are open from 7am to 10pm local time. A government needs 61 of 120 seats, and polls show neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition clearly reaching that number (Al Jazeera, 20 Oct). Why it matters: the result could shape Israel's role in the wider Gulf conflict, which is keeping oil above $100 a barrel.

items.title: HSBC slides after results; FTSE 100 down 0.9% in early trade
items.summary: HSBC's third-quarter pre-tax profit rose 32% to $9.6 billion, in line with the bank's compiled forecasts, and it announced another buyback of up to $1 billion, but wealth revenue was flat at $2.7 billion after 15% and 23% growth in the first two quarters; the shares fell 5% in Hong Kong (Reuters via The Star, 27 Oct). In London the FTSE 100 fell 94 points, or 0.9%, to 10,673 in early Tuesday trade from Monday's close of 10,767.33, and the FTSE 250 was down 46 points at 24,455 (Share Talk, 27 Oct, 09:19 UTC).

items.title: Fed meeting starts; markets price an 82% chance of a December hike
items.summary: Traders price about an 11% chance of a Fed rate hike at this week's meeting and an 82% chance of an increase in December, according to the CME FedWatch tool (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 27 Oct). The decision is on Wednesday at 20:00 SAST. On Monday the S&P 500 closed at 7,676.77, the Nasdaq at 26,169.38 and the Dow at 52,361.58 (Reuters via Business Recorder, 26 Oct close).

items.title: Asia: Nikkei up 2.2% and KOSPI up 3.6% at midday on the chip rally
items.summary: At midday on Tuesday the Nikkei 225 was up 2.2% at 63,542.77 and the KOSPI up 3.6% at 5,667.99, while the Hang Seng slipped 0.2% to 23,174.44 and the Shanghai Composite 0.1% to 3,692.58 (AP via WSB Radio, 27 Oct).

items.title: Results today: Visa after the close, Coca-Cola before the open
items.summary: Coca-Cola reports before the US open and Visa after the close on Tuesday 27 October; HSBC also reports today (Nasdaq earnings calendar, 26 Oct). Microsoft and Alphabet follow on Wednesday and Amazon on Thursday.

items.title: SA leading indicator rises 1.1% in August; rand steady near R16.65/$
items.summary: The SARB's leading business cycle indicator rose 1.1% month on month in August after a 0.8% fall in July (Newsquawk, 27 Oct). The index tracks items such as vehicle sales, business confidence and money supply; one month's rise can be revised or reversed. Before the release the rand was at 16.6525 to the dollar, little changed, and the 2035 government bond yield was 8.62% (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 27 Oct).

items.title: Moody's seen as most likely to upgrade South Africa, possibly within a year
items.summary: After Moody's called the medium-term budget 'credit positive', Business Day reports an upgrade from Ba2 (positive outlook since May) could come within about a year. Bank of America sees Moody's as the most likely agency to act, possibly to Ba1, and calls an S&P move to BB+ 'a closer call'; Investec's Annabel Bishop expects a Moody's upgrade in about 18 months, and Treasury says Moody's and S&P could upgrade within 12 to 18 months. Moody's and S&P review South Africa on 27 November and Fitch on 11 December. Moody's says a track record of fiscal delivery still has to be built (Business Day, 27 Oct). No rating action has been announced.

items.title: JSE shrugs off Brazil's crash; rand near R16.64/$
items.summary: The JSE All Share closed at 109,130.32 on Monday, up about 1.0% from Friday's 108,020.10, and the Top 40 at 100,977.01, up about 1.0% (Yahoo Finance via LRC Market Dashboard, 26 Oct). Brazil's Ibovespa closed down 13.88% at 176,608 and the dollar rose about 8.4% to near R$5.41 after Lula's re-election (Rio Times, 26 Oct). The rand was at 16.6371 to the dollar early on Tuesday, against 16.6125 on Monday morning (Yahoo Finance, 27 Oct; Reuters via Channel Africa, 26 Oct).
items.source: Rio Times; Channel Africa (Reuters); Yahoo Finance

items.title: Brent eases to $114.80 on Iran diplomacy; gold briefly below $4,000
items.summary: Brent crude for December fell 0.87% to $114.80 a barrel on Tuesday as renewed diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war raised hopes of de-escalation; losses were limited because Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continued over the weekend and President Trump said he was weighing a deal or more military action (Reuters via CNBC Africa, 27 Oct). Spot gold slipped to $3,999.81 an ounce on Tuesday morning, down 0.42% (TokenPost, 27 Oct), and COMEX gold futures were at $4,029.70, down 0.22% (CNBC TV18, 27 Oct). Earlier, at 00:53 GMT, platinum was at $1,529.27 (Investing.com, 27 Oct).

items.title: Dollar firm; yen weaker before Bank of Japan decision
items.summary: The dollar index was at 102.05 (+0.09%), the yen at 157.73 per dollar, EUR/USD at 1.1172 and GBP/USD at 1.3342 on Tuesday morning in Asia. The Bank of Japan is expected to hold at 1.25% on Friday (Investing.com, 27 Oct).

items.title: MSFT: Microsoft offers buyouts to about 60,000 staff a day before results
items.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees at vice-president level and below on selected teams in the US, Canada, India and the UK, with some data-centre, sales and marketing staff excluded; the package is 'similar to a standard severance offer' and the company expects fewer takers than for a July retirement-age offer (Bloomberg via Investing.com, 26 Oct). That is roughly a quarter of the 223,000 staff it had at the end of June. Microsoft closed at $532.60 on Monday, up 1.5% (LRC Stock Scanner, 26 Oct close), and reports results on Wednesday 28 October. MSFT is a HOLD on the LRC Stock Scanner, held back by the LRC Analyst Target of $513.80 (about 4% below the price); rating unchanged.

items.title: KO and V: results today; GOOGL tomorrow
items.summary: Coca-Cola reports before the US open and Visa after the close today, and Alphabet on Wednesday (Nasdaq earnings calendar, 26 Oct). On the LRC Stock Scanner KO ($92.70) and V ($404.20) are HOLD, both held back by LRC Analyst Targets below the price, and GOOGL ($316.80) is a BUY (LRC Stock Scanner, 26 Oct close); ratings unchanged.

items.title: META and NVDA: Nvidia to invest $3 billion in Meta; stock priced at $625
items.summary: Nvidia will buy $3 billion of the stock offering Meta announced on Monday, as part of a wider partnership on Meta's Muse agent platform and models (Axios, 27 Oct). Meta priced $25 billion of common stock at $625 a share, up from a $22.5 billion target, alongside $12.5 billion of mandatory convertible preferred; Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom were named as anchor investors, and the offerings are expected to close on 29 October (TokenPost, 27 Oct). The $625 price is about 2.8% below Monday's close of $642.70 (LRC Stock Scanner, 26 Oct close). Meta also plans wider use of Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform. META and NVDA are BUY on the LRC Stock Scanner; ratings unchanged.

items.title: NVIDIA: Asian chip rally follows Monday's 2.4% gain
items.summary: NVIDIA closed up 2.39% at $216.00 on Monday (Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct), and chip stocks extended gains in Asia on Tuesday, with the KOSPI up more than 4% (Reuters via Business Recorder, 27 Oct). Results are due on 17 November. NVDA is a BUY on the LRC Stock Scanner; rating unchanged.
